articles.title: Celtic - Celta en directo | Última hora de Europa League en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Hello there.... y bienvenidos al partido de la jornada para nostálgicos y amantes del futbol incluso boomer, ese Celtic-Celta, que comparten algo más
articles.body:
Última hora del Celtic - Celta, en directo:

Hay varios lazos de unión entre el Celta y el Celtic, que abarcan el mundo de la cultura y la tradición. Esos orígenes celtas por los que el club vigués tenía la intención de que el conjunto escocés formase parte de la programación de su centenario con la disputa de un partido amistoso que al final no llegó a celebrarse.

Por este motivo, el partido ha despertado una tremenda expectación entre los seguidores célticos, que de forma masiva ocuparán las gradas del Celtic Park. Serán 3000 los celtistas que se desplacen a Glasgow, cifra semejante a la del viaje de la pasada temporada a Lyon, y por encima de la de hace 10 años a Old Trafford para medirse al Manchester United.

Un partido en el que los seguidores más radicales del Celtic, enfrentados con la propiedad del club, anuncian un plante en el encuentro ante el cuadro de Claudio Giráldez. Dos equipos que necesitan los puntos en juego, al contar por derrotas los dos partidos disputados hasta la fecha en la fase de grupos.

No será la primera vez que en Europa se vean las caras Celtic y Celta. Se midieron en la tercera ronda de la Copa de la UEFA de la temporada 2002-03. En el Celtic Park vencieron los escoceses por 1-0 y en Balaídos lo haría el cuadro que entonces dirigía Miguel Ángel Lotina por 2-1. Se clasificó el Celtic por el valor doble de los goles en campo contrario. Aquella temporada los célticos se clasificarían para disputar Champions League.

Para el Celta, Escocia tiene un vínculo sentimental a mayores. Su primera participación en Europa, hace de ello ya 55 años, fue ante el Aberdeen.

articles.title: Sri Lanka make 430 to beat England after Brook's 202
articles.summary: Harry Brook’s first double century by an England batter in a one-day international is not enough to prevent his team being stunned by Sri Lanka, who pull off...
articles.body:
One-day international tri-series, Rawalpindi

England 429-4 (50 overs): Brook 202, Root 69, Jacks 66*

Sri Lanka 430-8 (49.5 overs): Rathnayake 130, Avishka 97, Shanaka 97

Harry Brook's first double century by an England batter in a one-day international was not enough to prevent his team being stunned by Sri Lanka, who pulled off a remarkable chase of 430 in Rawalpindi.

Brook passed Ben Stokes' previous England best score of 182 and posted the fastest ODI double hundred, off 114 balls, in his astonishing 202.

In clobbering the 14th double-hundred in a men's one-day international and the 12th highest individual score, Brook lifted England to 429-4 – at halfway the highest total made in a one-day international in Pakistan.

But Sri Lanka, who chose to bat second, were not deterred, even when they were reduced to 24-2. They set about completing the second-highest successful chase in ODI history.

Pavan Rathnayake made a sublime 130, while Aviksha Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both added 97.

With Jofra Archer rested for the tri-series and leg-spinner Adil Rashid left out of this match for tactical reasons, England's bowling was woeful. Sam Curran conceded 103 runs from his nine overs.

Up with the required rate throughout their innings, Sri Lanka needed 109 from the final 10 overs and were able to absorb the losses of Rathnayake and Shanaka.

Sri Lanka needed eight off the final over, sent down by Josh Tongue, who was pinpoint with his accuracy to bowl Dinuth Wellalage and Eshan Malinga with successive deliveries.

But in a sensational finish, Janith Liyanage, the man bowling when Brook reached 200, would not be denied.

With six needed from two balls, Liyanage pummelled Tongue's penultimate delivery of the match down the ground for a match-winning maximum, sparking joyous Sri Lankan celebrations.

One of the most incredible one-day internationals ever played ended with an aggregate of 847 runs, behind only a match total of 872 when South Africa chased 435 to beat Australia in 2006.

The total of 123 boundaries across both innings - 93 fours and 30 sixes - is also a record in ODIs.

How did England lose this game? At halfway, when Brook left the field arm-in-arm with Will Jacks, the thought of Sri Lanka even getting close to their target seemed highly fanciful.

Yet, Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis' decision to chase proved inspired, despite the way his team were dismantled by Brook.

Ultimately, Sri Lanka put the conditions – and Brook's knock – into context, helped by an England team who wilted under the pressure.

They were hampered by the dew, another factor in Sri Lanka's decision to bat second. England made mistakes in the field and their bowlers struggled to grip the ball. Without Archer, they lacked a death bowler.

And, with less then a year to go until the World Cup, England showed no composure as the game began to run away from them.

For as well as Brook batted, his tactics will come into question. Too much faith was placed in Curran, whose 103-2 are the most expensive figures returned by an England bowler in an ODI.

Gus Atkinson opened the bowling and sent down just seven overs of his allotted 10 and Tongue, who almost rescued the game, was only into his ninth.

This tri-series is designed to replicate the tournament conditions England will face at the World Cup in southern Africa. Two games in they are without a win and facing the prospect of needing to beat Pakistan in Lahore on Sunday to stay in the competition.

Brook has become the first man in ODI history to make a double hundred and end up on the losing side.

His strokeplay was irresistible. In a 116-ball stay, he mixed innovation with brutal power and deft touches. He scored all around the ground, clearing the ropes for 10 sixes and adding 21 fours.

A feature of Brook's knock was his measured acceleration. The 27-year-old had only 13 runs from the first 24 deliveries he faced, then upped the pace to reach 50 from 42 balls. His century, his fourth in ODIs, was completed in 75 balls.

It was upon reaching three figures that Brook really cut loose. He went from 100 to 200 in only 39 balls.

As England added 156 in the final 10 overs, Brook passed Stokes' record with a six whipped over the leg side off a full toss bowled by left-arm seamer Dilshan Madushanka.

Whether he was aware of the milestone or not, Brook did not acknowledge his achievement and, in the same over, was dropped at mid-off on 185.

Brook began the final over, delivered by seamer Liyanage, on 186. He clobbered the first ball over the covers for six, then scampered back for two unlikely twos.

Fittingly, the double hundred was reached with a paddled-sweep, then he was caught at third man off the final ball of the innings.

Somehow, it was not enough. Liyanage had the final say.

articles.title: The SEC is a beautiful mess. Texas and Ole Miss are about to find out who can survive it
articles.summary: Ole Miss vs. Texas is essentially an SEC title elimination game for the loser.
articles.body:
Australians have a phrase called the "tall poppy syndrome," where the tallest flower is the one that gets clipped. Fishermen point to crabs in a bucket, where no one crab can climb out before the rest drag it back down. The SEC's version is the 2026 schedule, where after seven turbulent weeks, the only thing we know is that we don't know anything.

Only three teams — Texas A&M, Arkansas and Vanderbilt — can't lay claim to a transitive conference lead. (A&M has just one conference win, over Arkansas; Arkansas has one, over Vandy; and Vandy has none over anybody.) Everybody else, from conference leader Georgia to — wait, is this right? — conference co-leader Kentucky, can claim they beat somebody who beat somebody who beat somebody who beat the biggest dog (or Dawg) in the yard.

Which leads us to an overwhelming question: Who's in line to head to Atlanta for the SEC championship? And as it turns out, this weekend might just be the first de facto play-in game.

No. 7 Ole Miss travels to Austin to face No. 19 Texas in one of only two ranked matchups this weekend. (No. 14 Houston at No. 10 Utah is the other.) Given that both Ole Miss and Texas have lost to Florida — and Texas lost to Oklahoma, too — this is virtually a loser-leaves-town game for the right to play in the SEC championship and earn its sweet, sweet automatic playoff berth.

For Texas, the stakes are existential. The Longhorns' comeback victory over then-No. 1 Ohio State is a long way back and growing smaller in the rear-view mirror every week. The much-more-recent losses to the Gators and Sooners loom far larger, as does the sense that the entire season is leaking oil.

The put-up-or-shut-up moment for Texas, head coach Steve Sarkisian and would-be prince Arch Manning has arrived . A third straight loss, again in front of the home crowd, would effectively detonate Texas' CFP hopes, and might just set in motion a regime change. (Yes, this is purely speculation, but patience is wearing thin in Austin.)

Ole Miss is the more fascinating case here, because nobody's quite sure what to make of the Rebels. Are they the team that threw LSU out of Vaught-Hemingway Stadium back in September? Are they the team that somehow forgot that defense is part of the game in giving up 52 points to Florida just two weeks later? Or, like every other erratic SEC team, are they both?

Head coach Pete Golding broke down the elusive concept of consistency over the course of a long season earlier this week. "Number one's good players, number two's stability and system, and number three is the ability to hold them accountable," he said. "That's the toughest piece, that third one. When they come off of a really emotional win, and the ability to refocus and know, man, we got to do it again. Sometimes there's a false confidence that's created based on outcomes. … There's some things that we've gotten away with that we're about to play a really elite football team that we're not [going to get away with]."

Trinidad Chambliss continues to pace the Rebels; Ole Miss ranks second in the SEC (to LSU) and 13th overall in passing offense. But Ole Miss is aggressively ordinary in scoring offense, ranking 7th in the SEC and 19th overall, and far worse in scoring defense, tied at 72nd with East Carolina and just above Georgia State. All due respect to the Pirates and Panthers, but that's not exactly national championship territory yet. There's still work to be done, and Ole Miss' schedule will provide exactly that.

After Texas, Ole Miss has five games remaining on the schedule, and only one of them could remotely be considered a cakewalk — the pre-Thanksgiving tuneup against Wofford. The Rebels will face unpredictable Auburn, potentially lethal Georgia and who-even-knows Oklahoma before wrapping the regular season with Mississippi State in the always-strange Egg Bowl. Ole Miss could make that run with five wins or it could end the regular season with two, and given how this season has gone so far, it wouldn't be a real shock either way.

Ole Miss was just 18 seconds away from a berth in last year's title game; only a late Carson Beck scramble propelled Miami past the Rebels. Golding and the Rebels aren't hearing any title talk, and that's largely because of that Florida loss, as well as the usual blue-chip bias. But these are new days in the SEC and in college football, and Ole Miss stands in a perfect position to take advantage of the instability … starting this weekend.

articles.title: FIFA picks the US as host of the first Women’s Club World Cup in 2028
articles.summary: ZURICH (AP) — The United States will host the inaugural FIFA Women’s Club World Cup in 2028, soccer's governing body said Thursday.FIFA said the tournament f...
articles.body:
ZURICH (AP) — The United States will host the inaugural FIFA Women's Club World Cup in 2028, soccer's governing body said Thursday.

FIFA said the tournament featuring 19 of the best women's clubs from around the world will take place Jan. 5–30 in 2028, but did not announce host cities. The Women's Club World Cup will be staged every four years after that.

Seven clubs have already qualified for the inaugural event, FIFA said.

They include England's Arsenal, Spain's Barcelona, Mexico's América, Gotham FC from the U.S., Corinthians from Brazil, China's Wuhan Jiangda and Naegohyang from North Korea.

FIFA said it opted to return to the U.S. following the successful hosting of both this year's men's World Cup and the men's Club World Cup in 2025.

"Ultimately, the United States' recent excellence in staging top FIFA tournaments, combined with the significant interest in women's football there plus its elite sporting infrastructure, made the country the standout option." FIFA chief women's football officer Sarai Bareman said.

articles.title: FIFA’s new U-15 World Cup to feature 190 countries, nearly 1,000 games
articles.summary: The inaugural edition of the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival is set to kick off in Baku, Azerbaijan on Saturday, Oct. 24.
articles.body:
The inaugural edition of the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival is set to kick off in Baku, Azerbaijan on Saturday, Oct. 24.

The tournament is notable for its sheer scale. It is open to all 211 of FIFA's member associations, with 190 countries confirmed to participate.

Mexico and Canada will be among the nations representing Concacaf, but the United States won't send a team to the competition.

The tournament's size and lack of a qualifying requirement means that for many smaller countries, the week-long competition will be their first opportunity to compete on such a large stage.

For 78 countries, the tournament will mark the first time they will feature in a FIFA World Cup competition.

According to FIFA chief of global football development Arsene Wenger, the tournament presents a huge opportunity for players who may not otherwise get the chance to have their talent displayed at a global FIFA competition.

"Talent exists everywhere, but young players do not always have the same opportunities to test themselves internationally," the longtime Arsenal manager told FIFA's website.

"This tournament is about providing them with that opportunity. By bringing teams from across the world together at U-15 level, we can give players meaningful matches, expose them to different styles and football cultures, and help them learn and develop through competition."

With so many teams involved and nearly 1,000 matches scheduled, the tournament will take place in an 8v8 format with 20-minute halves.

The majority of the competition will take place at the custom-built Hovsan Competition Complex, which will stage as many as 20 simultaneous matches across multiple pitches.

The 2026 tournament will feature boys, while the first girls tournament is scheduled for 2027. Both girls' and boys' tournaments are then planned to take place annually starting in 2028.

articles.title: Lions turning to this veteran to replace Tom Kennedy at punt returner
articles.summary: Few players in the NFL have as much experience at returner than DeAndre Carter, who has a combined 299 kick and punt returns since 2015.
articles.body:
ALLEN PARK — The Detroit Lions have found their replacement for Tom Kennedy at kick and punt returner.

Special teams coordinator Dave Fipp said Thursday, Oct. 22, the Lions are "probably" turning to veteran DeAndre Carter, who on Monday signed with Detroit's practice squad. Carter, 33, entered the league as an undrafted free agent in 2015 out of Sacremento State. The Lions are his 11th team.

The Lions chose Carter over a handful of other options on their practice squad, including Dominic Lovett, Lucky Jackson and Lawrence Keys, each of whom have some level of experience at returner, whether that be in the NFL or the United Football League.

Kennedy went down with a season-ending knee injury in a win over the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 11.

Carter has 155 career punt returns for 1,508 yards, good for an average of 9.7 yards. As a kick returner, where he'll play next to Jacob Saylors with the Lions, he has 144 career attempts for 3,399 yards. Since the NFL changed its rules in 2024 to add the "dynamic kickoff," Carter has averaged 29 yards across 26 returns.

"I think DeAndre Carter has a lot of experience, he'll probably step in and return punts for us and kickoffs for us in the game (against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, Oct. 25), along with Saylors, and we'll just keep going as it's been," Fipp said. "Obviously, Lovett factors in to some degree. Lucky Jackson's had some experience doing it a little bit. None of those guys the same type of experience that DeAndre's had."

Fipp and Carter overlapped with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2018, when Fipp was the special teams coordinator and Carter made the initial roster coming out of training camp. After Darren Sproles got hurt, Carter began returning punts. He made seven appearances with the Eagles that season.

"I think he had gotten cut by like four teams," Fipp recalled of the 2018 season. "He had bounced around and kept on fighting, trying to make it. I think we were in Week 4 or something like that, I believe it was when Darren Sproles went down. He came in, we're playing against Tennessee, and he did what he does.

"He catches the ball, he competes, he gets downhill, he's quick, very competitive. His story is like the ultimate story of just overcoming all of the obstacles, and he plays the game that way. He loves playing football. I've always respected his game."

The Lions had Carter and Steven Sims, another veteran, in for tryouts Oct. 15. Fipp said it wasn't him who initially brought up Carter's name, but rather Detroit's pro personnel department. But of course, "I know a lot about him," Fipp said, "and I think he'll do a great job for us."

Carter also offers the ability to play receiver in a pinch. He's caught 117 of his 171 career targets for 1,331 yards and six touchdowns. His best season came with the Los Angeles Chargers in 2022, when he had 46 catches for 538 yards and three scores. In his next three seasons with the Las Vegas Raiders (2023), Chicago Bears (2024) and Cleveland Browns (2025), he had 111 yards on 13 receptions.

There are currently three open spots on the Lions' active roster. Two of those are reserved for safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist), both of whom are expected to be activated ahead of the Packers game. The third opening could go to Carter, or the Lions could choose to use a temporary elevation to bring him up from the practice squad.

▶ Series: Green Bay leads, 108-78-7 (Last meeting: Packers win, 31-24, on Nov. 27, 2025, in Detroit )

articles.title: Lionel Messi reflects on Barcelona career upon return to Spain for awards ceremony
articles.summary: Lionel Messi has headed back to Spain, where he will soon be awarded the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, prior to which he has taken the opportunity t...
articles.body:
Lionel Messi has returned, even if only briefly, to Spain, where he is set to be awarded the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports by King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia on Friday in Oviedo.

The 39-year-old striker, who recently retired from the Argentine national team in style back in Buenos Aires, has continued this nostalgic tour back in his longtime home of Spain, where he addressed, among numerous other topics, his legendary career with Barcelona.

In an interview with the EFE news agency, via ARA , Messi reflected, "We were lucky enough to win everything, also in the way we did it, in how we enjoyed playing, winning, achieving important things, but above all in how we enjoyed the day-to-day, the training sessions... We had a great time.

"It is hard to find words to explain everything that Barcelona means. Many good things happened there. I have a very, very special affection for the city, for the club."

After joining La Masia in 2000 from Newell's Old Boys, Messi went on to spend 21 years with La Blaugrana, winning 10 La Liga titles, seven Copa del Reys, and four UEFA Champions Leagues amongst numerous other accolades. He left the club in 2021 as their record holder in appearances, goals, and most goals in a single season, amongst others.

Following a brief stint with Paris Saint-Germain, Messi swapped Europe for North America, joining David Beckham's Inter Miami in 2023, which he still calls home.

Now an eight-time Ballon d'Or winner, as well as a FIFA World Cup winner, Argentina's record holder in appearances, goals, and assists said he hoped to be remembered "as a great athlete," as well as someone who consistently battled to accomplish their goals and dreams. "Sometimes it worked out for me, sometimes it didn't, but I never stopped trying to win everything that was in front of me."

With this in mind, Messi will soon join the likes of Serena Williams, Eliud Kipchoge, Lindsey Vonn, Xavi Hernández, Rafael Nadal, and Michael Schumacher in receiving the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

In a statement announcing Messi's selection for the award in July, the foundation wrote, "In addition to his dazzling talent, the Jury has highlighted his exceptional sporting career and his formidable and continued charitable work to promote access to education and health care for the most disadvantaged children.

"Leo Messi, the player who has won the most titles in the history of football, has also earned the respect and admiration of everyone for his exemplary behaviour on the field and for his consistency, humility and commitment to the team game."

Responding to the award, Messi said, "I would like to sincerely thank the Jury and the Princess of Asturias Foundation for this recognition, which is a huge source of pride for me. Spain and Catalonia are part of my life: I grew up there as a footballer, I lived there for many years, and my children were born there. I always felt a great deal of affection from people, which is why this award is so very special for me.

"I always say that I achieved nothing alone: behind every achievement there are fellow players, family and many people who helped me along the way. I hope my story inspires many boys and girls to keep dreaming, with hard work and love for the sport, and knowing that the most important thing is to try to be a good person and respect the values that sport teaches us."

articles.title: Women's Club World Cup: United States to host inaugural edition in 2028
articles.summary: Arsenal are named as one of the teams to compete at the inaugural Women's Club World Cup, to be hosted in the United States in 2028.
articles.body:
The United States will host the inaugural Women's Club World Cup in January 2028, Fifa has confirmed.

Arsenal have been named as one of seven teams set to play in the tournament, with a further 12 clubs to be determined at a later date.

The 19-team tournament, designed to echo the revamped men's Club World Cup and take place every four years, is scheduled from 5-30 January 2028.

The United States staged the men's Club World Cup in 2025 and co-hosted the men's World Cup this summer, with Mexico and Canada.

The country is also set to co-host the Women's World Cup with Costa Rica, Jamaica and Mexico in 2031.

"Ultimately, the United States' recent excellence in staging top Fifa tournaments, combined with the significant interest in women's football there plus its elite sporting infrastructure, made the country the standout option," said Fifa's chief women's football officer Sarai Bareman.

Barcelona, Gotham, Club America, Corinthians, Naegohyang and Wuhan Jiangda have also booked their place at the tournament.

Six more European clubs will be selected to represent Uefa, while there will be three clubs apiece for AFC (Asia), CAF (Africa), Concacaf (North America, Central America and the Caribbean) and Conmebol (South America), and one from OFC (Oceania).

"These seven clubs, and a dozen more, will come together to show the strength and depth of women's club football to a global audience," added Bareman.

"They will have the opportunity to tell their story, expand their fanbase and represent their club on the world stage. They have thoroughly earned this opportunity to be part of history in the United States."

Earlier this year, the Women's Super League described the scheduling of the Club World Cup as potentially "catastrophic".

It is the second mid-season women's competition to be introduced by Fifa in recent years - following the Champions Cup, which took place for the first time in February and was won by Arsenal.

articles.title: El Getafe llena de regalos al Lugano
articles.standfirst: Los azulones permitieron muchas facilidades y salen goleados ante su público
articles.summary: Los azulones permitieron muchas facilidades y salen goleados ante su público
articles.body: Un Getafe irreconocible, sobre todo en la primera mitad, se dejó sorprender por el Lugano para sufrir la primera derrota en la Conference League y seguir sin ganar en la tercera competición continental. Volvía el fútbol continental a Getafe, pero no fue un día de fiesta. Los de Bordalás no fueron fieles a lo que les pide su técnico y permitieron muchas facilidades al equipo suizo, que se puso las botas ante tanto regalo azulón. Desde 2016 no le metían una manita en casa, lo que deja claro que el Getafe no fue el Getafe. Se las prometían muy felices los locales cuando a los dos minutos y en su primera llegada, Iván Azón marcaba de lanzamiento lejano. La alegría duró apenas un minuto porque Ajeti lograba el empate en la primera aproximación del Lugano anotando con le pecho. La locura inicial no acabó ahí, porque a los siete minutos el Lugano ya mandaba en el marcador con el tanto de Cimignani en una jugada que evidenció los problemas del Getafe por la banda izquierda. Por ese mismo lado llegó la acción del tercero. Un balón por encima de la defensa al costado de Davinchi y un centro que remataba de primeras Ajeti para conseguir su doblete y abrir distancias. Demasiadas facilidades para un equipo tan rocoso como le Getafe, que pudo encajar el cuarto antes del descanso, pero Soria evitó el triplete de Ajeti. Era evidente que a Bordalás no le gustó nada la primera mitad. El Lugano controló el juego con facilidad y le desangró con los pases a la espada de la defensa. De ahí que el técnico alicantino hiciera cuatro cambios al descanso, tratando de cambiar cosas y dejando señalados a varios de sus jugadores que no estuvieron a la altura, sobre todo en la defensa, donde sustituyó a tres de los cuatro. De poco sirvió porque, a los cinco minutos de la reanudación, una mala salida de balón terminó en el cuarto, obra de Bislimi. Cualquier atisbo de reacción quedó desactivado rápidamente. Al Getafe no le quedó otra que seguir intentándolo y tuvo alguna llegada peligrosa. Bordalás también quiso buscar mayor pegada con la entrada de Enes Ünal, pero el turco se torció el tobillo derecho a los cinco minutos de entrar y, aunque continuó en el campo, lo lastró hasta el final. No era la tarde del Getafe, estaba claro. Pero el equipo no bajó los brazos y Borja Mayoral recortó distancias a un cuarto de hora del final con la colaboración del meta Von Ballmoos. El gol les dio alas porque siguieron insistiendo y a punto estuvieron de anotar en dos jugadas consecutivas. Una se fue lamiendo el poste y la otra se la sacó el portero a Gudelj con una gran estirada. También la tuvo Ünal en boca de gol, pero erró. Para errores, el de Ballo en otra mala salida de balón, que regaló el pase a Behrens para que se quedase solo e hiciera el quinto en el descuento. La derrota deja tocado al Getafe, que suma un punto de seis posibles y con muy malas sensaciones tras un encuentro que mostró la peor cara del equipo azulón justo antes de recibir a uno de los favoritos, el Mónaco.

articles.summary: Estos son los jugadores con más movimiento en Los 100 de MARCA de una temporada a otra
articles.body: Tras una nueva temporada futbolística que incluyó Copa del Mundo, el ranking de Los 100 de MARCA by Orange reconoce a los futbolistas más destacados del año. Como es habitual, hay jugadores que subieron posiciones mientras otros descendieron en la lista respecto a la edición anterior. Pero... ¿Quiénes han sido los más sobresalientes o los más dramáticos?. Lo repasamos a continuación. Las principales irrupciones las protagonizan Rodri y Kvaratskhelia. Ambos no estuvieron entre los nominados en la IV edición de Los 100 de MARCA y se han colocado en el top-5 en esta quinta, siendo solamente superados por Kane, Lamine Yamal y Mbappé. Rodri es cuarto y Kvaratskhelia, quinto. También destacan como 'novedades' dos nombres españoles que ocupan huecos en el top-20: Ferran Torres, autor del gol que dio el segundo Mundial a España, y Mikel Oyarzabal. Para Leo Messi es un 'subidón' total. El argentino, sexto clasificado, pasa del discreto 49 del pasado curso al top-10 de esta temporada. Su Mundial fue exquísito, liderando a Argentina hacia el subcampeonato... y con Inter Miami se proclamó campeón de la primera Major League Soccer de la historia de la franquicia. Que tenga 39 años parece una simple anécdota. Llaman la atención también otros nombres que suben como Harry Kane (del 12 al 1, llevándose Los 100 de MARCA esta temporada 2025-26), Michael Olise (sube 24 puestos), Erling Haaland (sube 29) o Jude Bellingham (sube 26). articles.title: Dylan Raiola to Start for Oregon After Benching, Latest Rumors with Dante Moore Out Injured
articles.summary: Dylan Raiola is reportedly Oregon's starting quarterback once again.
articles.body:
Dylan Raiola is reportedly Oregon's starting quarterback once again.

Pete Nakos of On 3 reported Thursday that Raiola is expected to start Saturday's game against Illinois in place of the injured Dante Moore. Moore has been out since he suffered a concussion during the Ducks' Sept. 26 win over USC, and Raiola was the initial replacement.

Oregon started Brock Thomas in the last game against Nebraska because of Raiola's struggles against UCLA before eventually turning back to Raiola in the fourth quarter.

It has been something of a roller-coaster ride for the Nebraska transfer ever since coming into the USC game following Moore's injury.

He led the Ducks to a high-profile victory in that one by going 19-of-25 for 289 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions and seemed to be the clear-cut answer at the position until Moore was ready to return.

However, it was a different story against the Bruins.

Raiola went 6-of-19 passing with two interceptions and a lost fumble before he was benched for Thomas, who nearly directed a comeback in the 17-15 loss. It wasn't surprising that Oregon went with Thomas for the following game against the Cornhuskers, but he struggled throughout the contest at 9-of-20 passing with an interception.

Just when it seemed like Oregon was going to pick up its third loss of the season, Raiola entered the game in the fourth quarter and directed a field goal drive on his first possession and a touchdown drive on his second.

He found Jamari Johnson with fewer than 30 seconds remaining for the game-winning touchdown that kept the Ducks alive in the College Football Playoff race.

Now Raiola will get another opportunity in a season with little margin for error after the team already lost games to Oklahoma State and UCLA. Another defeat could be the end of Oregon's playoff hopes, and it still has games remaining against Ohio State, Michigan and Northwestern.

But even those games will lose some of their importance if Raiola cannot deliver against Illinois.

articles.title: Lech Poznan 1-1 Sunderland: Timur Tutierov's first Black Cats goal not enough as dominant visitors punished in Poland
articles.summary: Match report as Sunderland are made to pay for missed chances and failing to make dominance count as Timur Tutierov's second-minute goal is cancelled out by Martin Bengtsson in 1-1 draw at Lech Poznan in Europa League
articles.body:
The 21-year-old got the Black Cats' - and his own - night off to the perfect start with the fastest goal in this season's Europa League, nodding home Nilson Angulo's cross with barely a minute gone after Mateusz Lis' poor clearance was picked off.

Tutierov spent last season on loan in League One with Exeter and was playing just his fourth game for Sunderland, having been fast-tracked into the club's first team following injuries to Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor.

After a brief response from the hosts and a couple of gilt-edged chances, the Black Cats threatened to add to their lead and hit the post through Angulo, but a host of chances came and went without adding to their early opener. They would end up registering 25 shots, including 11 on target, but it was not enough.

Having lost both of their opening league-phase games 4-0, Lech finally registered their first goal in Europe this season when substitute Martin Bengtsson fired through a crowd of bodies following a knock-down from a corner to beat an unsighted Robin Roefs at his near post with 20 minutes to go.

Though Sunderland pushed to restore their lead and saw substitute Chris Rigg curl a 20-yard effort inches over the bar, they were made to pay for failing to make their dominance count as they were denied victory for the first time in their European campaign, but remain unbeaten in the Europa League following a seventh point from their three matches so far.

2: GOAL! Tutierov scores the fastest goal in this season's Europa League, heading home Angulo's cross when Sunderland press high and force a mistake from Lis.

3: CHANCE! Roefs has to be at his best to make a superb double save from Radoslaw Murawski after initially spilling Patrik Walemark's shot into his path.

16: BIG CHANCE! Daniel Hakans races through from Pablo Rodriguez's pass in behind but misses the target altogether past a sprawling Roefs.

21: OFF THE POST! When Granit Xhaka's shot is tipped away, Fofana strikes the outside of the far post from a tight angle.

70: GOAL! Sunderland are punished for not making their dominance count as substitute Bengtsson fires in an equaliser following a corner.

82: SO CLOSE! Rigg is inches away from restoring Sunderland's lead but can only lift a curling effort onto the roof of the net from 20 yards.

"Really open. We started really well I think. We expected this atmosphere and this style of play from our opponent. I think they are a good team.

"After the first goal, they showed they have quality to build up under pressure, to go through our block when we were a bit open. They created chances as well.

"After that we created our own chances and I think we deserved to score the second goal, but we didn't. In a stadium like this, against a good team, the momentum can switch really quickly and it happened.

"It was a good experience. We started the game with seven players who were under 23-years-old so they need to experience those situations, intense against a good team to get better."

Analysis: Familiar woes deny Sunderland victory

"Sunderland have found goals hard to come by this season, notching only six in seven Premier League games, and had only themselves to blame again as they scored just once against a team who had shipped eight in their previous two league-phase games.

"There are mitigating factors with the absence of Wilson Isidor and Brian Brobbey, but that will not alleviate the growing sense of frustration from edging past Portuguese second-division side Torreense last week, being soundly beaten by Bournemouth and then being held by the team ranked bottom of the league phase at the start of match day three.

"The good news is that both Brobbey and Isidor are not far from a return, while Timur Tutierov's goal will do him the world of good after being thrown in at the deep end in his first Sunderland appearances - and finding life difficult."

articles.title: Juego, set en blanco y partido para la Real
articles.standfirst: Un equipo txuriurdin de nuevo muy eficaz superó con muchísima comodidad a un Lillestrom que al inicio de cada parte tuvo sus opciones, pero que terminó goleado
articles.summary: Un equipo txuriurdin de nuevo muy eficaz superó con muchísima comodidad a un Lillestrom que al inicio de cada parte tuvo sus opciones, pero que terminó goleado
articles.body: La Real Sociedad logró en Lillestrom su primera victoria en esta fase Liga de una Europa League en la que sigue soñando con llegar muy lejos, sobre todo con la moral que le dará el 0-6 que firmó, en una nueva exhibición de juego de ataque y eficacia de cara a la portería rival. La Real se llevó el primer susto a los 45 segundos tan sólo de juego, con un remate cercano de Olsen que salió por poco por encima de la portería de Marrero, que de inmediato vio como Jon Martín despejó el derechazo de Nyheim, cuando iba dirección gol. El equipo de Matarazzo intentó hacerse con la pelota, pero le costó llevar la iniciativa ante unos noruegos muy descarados, al defender muy lejos de su área sin ella y querer siempre hacer peligro con la pelota, como Paintsil con un remate cercano cruzado que se perdió a un par de metros del poste izquierdo. Cuando el gol local parecía mucho más cerca que el txuriurdin, Oyarzabal apareció para servirle un buen balón a Sergio Gómez, que con un zurdazo subió el 0-1 al electrónico. El 10 iba a volver a realizar un jugadón con otro pase de gol al 17, que amplió la renta solamente dos minutos más tarde. La cosa no quedó ahí, porque el campeón del Mundo hizo su tercera asistencia para el 0-3 de Sucic. Olsen lo volvió a intentar antes del descanso, pero sin puntería. Odegaard padre recurrió en el descanso a Kitolano y el recién incorporado a los 20 segundos chutó a portería, pero desviado. Olsen luego tiró de veteranía para sacar un penalti, pero Marrero se lo detuvo al ariete, que luego no encontró portería con un testarazo. A Ibrahimaj se le fue su buen disparo al larguero, en otro mejor comienzo local, como el de la primera mitad, y como entonces Óskarsson no perdonó en la primera que tuvo nada más sustituir a Oyarzabal y puso el 0-4. El 0-4 no llevó al Lillestrom a rendirse y Nyheim rozó el larguero con un cabezazo en un córner. Como si esperase a que le golpeasen para golpear, Sucic hizo el 0-5 aprovechando un error local en salida del balón, después de que a Óskarsson se le fuera la pelota lamiendo un palo. El islandés tuvo el sexto, pero se lo paró el portero noruego, que no llegó pese a su estirada a un zurdazo de Zakharyan por la escuadra. Olsen, por los locales, y Guedes y Zakharyan, por los txuriurdin, tuvieron las últimas, pero el 0-6 parecía un resultado muy bonito para variarlo.

articles.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Can Bayern’s Harry Kane end England’s 25 years of hurt?
articles.summary: Bayern Munich striker Kane faces tough competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe, who are also in the ‌‌running.
articles.body:
When the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony gets under way at the London Palladium this Monday, much of England will hope it serves as a good omen.

After all, the English haven’t seen one of their own lift the golden ball – football’s most prestigious individual award – in 25 years.

Michael Owen was the embodiment of English pride when he won the accolade in 2001. Now, it is Harry Kane who could bring his nation an honour every footballer dreams of.

So, what are Kane’s odds of winning the Ballon d’Or? Al Jazeera takes a look:

The best season of Kane’s career bodes well for Ballon d’Or

Remember the time when Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo scored 50-plus goals for fun? When a football forward’s goal tally looked more like a batsman’s cricket score?

Kane’s 2025-26 goal-scoring exploit is the closest we have experienced to that in recent years.

The England captain’s 73-goal performance last season was the finest display the world has seen since Argentinian legend Messi’s 82-goal tally in 2011-12.

“I’ve never liked to talk about myself too much,” Kane said in an interview last month.

“The only thing I would say is that last season was incredible, on a personal level and as a team.

“It was, by far, the best season of my life.”

Age is no problem for England and Bayern Munich’s Kane

He scored an incredible 36 goals last season, making Kane the Bundesliga’s top scorer for the third year running and earning him a second European Golden Shoe, while finishing nine goals clear of Manchester City’s Erling Haaland in the continental race.

The Bayern Munich forward’s statistics look even more impressive given he is seemingly peaking at 33, an age when most forwards are far beyond their prime.

Kane is bidding to join the ranks of Messi, Luka Modric and Karim Benzema, some of the recipients of the last 10 editions who won the Ballon d’Or in their 30s.

Standing in his way, however, are two very talented juniors – Spain’s superstar-in-the-making, Lamine Yamal, who won the 2026 FIFA World Cup shortly after his 19th birthday, and France’s 2018 world champion, Kylian Mbappe, who is 27.

When Kane made his Premier League debut for Tottenham Hotspur in 2014, Yamal was still in primary school, and Mbappe was in high school.

Could Champions League and World Cup woes hurt Kane’s bid?

Since Kane moved from London to Munich, the forward has taken German club football by storm, and 2025-26 was no different. He finished the campaign with three trophies: the Bundesliga title, DFB-Pokal (the German Cup) and Franz Beckenbauer Supercup (the German Supercup).

But his failure to make an impact in the Champions League semifinal cost Bayern Europe’s most coveted club trophy, and the same was the case at the recent World Cup, where he finished third with England .

While World Cup success is not a strict requirement to win the Ballon d’Or, having a world title on your CV definitely helps. Furthermore, being pitted against 2026 World Cup winners Yamal and Rodri – also the 2024 Ballon d’Or recipient – could hurt Kane’s odds.

Recent history suggests that winning a title in one of the major tournaments has become almost a prerequisite.

Only four of the previous 19 Ballon d’Or winners failed to lift either the Champions League, World Cup, European Championship or Copa America during the year they won the honour.

Those exceptions include record eight-time Ballon d’Or recipient Messi and five-time winner Ronaldo.

Kane is the bookmakers’ favourite to win the Ballon d’Or

Only time will tell whether falling short in major competitions’ crucial knockout rounds will decide Kane’s fate, but for now, he is the bookmakers’ leading candidate for the trophy.

As of Tuesday, Kane holds about 65-70 percent market share to become the successor to Ousmane Dembele, the 2025 Ballon d’Or winner.

Unlike other Ballon d’Or contenders, especially the outspoken Yamal and Mbappe, who are campaigning hard for the award, Kane has been relatively quiet.

Bayern are speaking up for their leader, having put together a video in which teammates said Kane should win.

“He deserves to win it, 100 percent, without a doubt,” said Colombian Luis Diaz, who is also on the shortlist.

If Kane wins the award, he would become only the fifth English player to do so after Stanley Matthews, Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen.

articles.title: Pichichi Javi Rodríguez: "Ni me lo creo aún, y además dos goles"
articles.standfirst: Tres goles y una asistencia en cuatro días
articles.summary: Tres goles y una asistencia en cuatro días
articles.body: Javi Rodríguez está de dulce. Hizo los dos goles de la remontada céltica en Glasgow, cuatro días después de haber marcado y asistido ante el Alavés en Balaídos. Tres goles que igualan su mejor cifra realizadora en la primera plantilla, los cuales consiguió en su temporada de debut hace dos años.... La pasada campaña no vio puerta. La renovación y la recuperación de sus dolencias le han sentado francamente bien al internacional, un futbolista que siempre ha sido clave para Claudio Giráldez y que ha recuperado su mejor versión. "Veníamos a un campo de Europa de los bonitos, ni me lo creo aún, y además dos goles, y viniendo de otro el fin de semana, y mira primeros tres puntos dando la vuelta la partido. ¿Que me pongan de nueve? Yo soy defensa, valgo para hacer lo de siempre y si puedo marcar y ayudar,. mejor", señaló al acabar el partido "Desde el calentamiento ya vimos y sentimos a los 3.000 aficionados, que era un partido importante tras dos malos resultados que lo hicimos sin jugar mal y esperemos ahora lograr más puntos desde ahora" Dos goles que sirvieron para que el Celta sumase sus tres primeros puntos en la fase de grupos, tras las derrotas ante Omonia Nicosia y Juventus y que sirve para ir enderezando la situación clasificatoria. Lo hicieron, además, en un estadio mítico. Ahora aparcarán durante dos semanas la Europa League, hasta la visita a Balaídos de la Union Saint-Gilloise. El Celta no estuvo solo en Celtic Park. Tres mil seguidores les arroparon desde la grada, dando colorido desde las horas previas y animando sin cesar durante todo el partido. Un desplazamiento a ls altura del de hace una década en Manchester o la pasada temporada en Lyon. Hubo cuatro permutas en el once de Claudio Giráldez con la entrada en el mismo de Marcos Alonso, Aleix Febas, Javi Rueda y el capitán Iago Aspas, que no era titular desde el pasado 7 de septiembre en el encuentro ante el Getafe.

articles.title: Freiburg suffers heavy defeat to Monaco ahead of Bayern clash
articles.summary: Freiburg couldn't build on their win in the Conference League season opener and were beaten 3-0 at Monaco on Thursday. Last season's Europa League runners-up...
articles.body:
Freiburg couldn't build on their win in the Conference League season opener and were beaten 3-0 at Monaco on Thursday.

Last season's Europa League runners-up started this term with a 3-2 win against Jablonec, but failed to repeat their success.

The hosts took the lead shortly before the break after collecting Mio Backhaus' careless ball reposition. Paris Brunner then flicked the ball over Max Rosenfelder before going on a run and slotting it home.

It took them a while, but Monaco were again on target in the 83rd. Ansu Fati's shot was well saved by Backhaus, but the rebound fell to Lamine Camara, who fired it home.

Fati got one himself in stoppage-time, lashing home into the bottom corner and completing the big win.

Freiburg will have to move one quickly as they have a Bundesliga table-topper against league leaders Bayern Munich on Sunday.

articles.title: Kramaric shines as Hoffenheim stun Lyon in the Europa League
articles.summary: Andrej Kramaric had a brilliant evening as Hoffenheim stunned Ligue 1 leaders Lyon in a 3-0 triumph on Thursday to claim their first win in the Europa League...
articles.body:
Andrej Kramaric had a brilliant evening as Hoffenheim stunned Ligue 1 leaders Lyon in a 3-0 triumph on Thursday to claim their first win in the Europa League this season.

The Germans took the lead shortly before the break as Tim Lemperle's throw-in was loose inside the box until the ball found Kramaric, who headed it into the goal.

Adam Daghim then doubled their advantage in the 49th. Kramaric received the ball near the penalty area and passed it to the left, where Noham Kamara accidentally set up Daghim, who cleverly slotted the ball into the lower-left corner.

Hoffenheim were finally able to celebrate the three points once Adam Hložek sealed the win in the 83rd. The German side intercepted a sloppy pass from Lyon and the ball again ended up with Kramaric, who served Hložek's effort.

The victory comes as huge relief for Hoffenheim. Before Thursday's game, they had only won three out of nine games in all competitions - none of them in the Europa League.

articles.title: De Winter y Maignan condenan al Milan
articles.standfirst: El Bournemouth no desaprovechó las concesiones del conjunto 'rossonerro'
articles.summary: El Bournemouth no desaprovechó las concesiones del conjunto 'rossonerro'
articles.body: La derrota contra el Benfica en la primera jornada de Europa League era la única que se le computaba al Milan en este primer tramo de temporada. A su paso por el sur de Inglaterra, sin embargo, el Bournemouth le hizo pagar (3-0) cada error. No habían pasado ni cinco minutos de partido cuando Evanilson se impuso en el corazón del área y, tras orientar su remate a la cabeza, De Winter sacó la mano a pasear y cometió penalti. Se lo pidió un especialista consumado desde los once metros como Justin Kluivert y, como suele ser habitual, no perdonó. Todavía más grosero fue la 'cruzada de cable' de Maignan antes de llegar a la primera media hora de encuentro. El meta galo a la salida de un saque de esquina, cometió una agresión sobre Tyler Adams en su intento por quitárselo de encima. El colegiado, tras consultar con el VAR, no sólo señaló penalti... sino que también le expulsó. Entró Torriani y, esta vez, fue Tavernier el encargado de duplicar la ventaja. El Milan estaba herido... pero el Bournemouth tampoco apretó en exceso en busca de hacer sangre. A cinco minutos para el final, sin embargo, Amine Adli conectó un 'misil' de falta que Torriani, prácticamente, no vio salir del pie izquierdo del atacante francomarroquí. Duro golpe para los de Amorim, que se quedan con tres puntos tras tres jornadas. El Besiktas está siendo un hueso duro de roer en esta Europa League. Se impuso a Marsella, Hoffenheim y, cuando parecía que todo estaba perdido, logró sacar un valioso empate frente al Crystal Palace (2-2). Yéremy Pino, con incertidumbre, logró igualar el tanto anotado por Ndidi en el descuento de la primera parte nada más volver del descanso. Mateta, a quien le anularon un gol nada más arrancar, convirtió el 1-2. En el 73', sin embargo, Olaitan conectó un 'latigazo' que frustró la remontada de los 'eagles'. El estreno, saldado con una derrota ante el OFI Creta, no fue el esperado. Pero, a partir de ahí, Imanol Alguacil cuenta sus partidos por victorias a los mandos de su nuevo Olympiacos. La última, por la mínima, frente al Sparta Praga (1-0). El gol llegó a poco más de 10' para el final: Pedersen centró desde el costado derecho y Armando González resolvió picando de cabeza contra el suelo. Benfica continúa intratable en esta Europa League. Lidera la clasificación por diferencia de goles respecto a Leverkusen, Bournemouth, Ferencvaros y Olympiacos. Todo, gracias a la goleada endosada a un Omonia (1-4) que llegó a igualar el tanto inicial de Echeverri. Tras el descanso, Pavlidis, Aursnes y Prestianni no dieron opción. El Hoffenheim, que había arrancado con dos derrotas frente a OFI y Besiktas, se desquitó pegándose un 'festín' ante su público contra el Olympique de Lyon (3-0). Kramaric, con un sutil remate de cabeza por encima de Greif, calmó los ánimos antes del descanso. A la vuelta, Daghim duplicó la ventaja y, ya en el 83', Hlozek terminó de sentenciar el triunfo.

articles.title: Dream night for Bournemouth - how did the Premier League come to dominate Europe?
articles.summary: Bournemouth's 3-0 win against AC Milan further illustrated the dominance of Premier League sides against their European counterparts.
articles.body:
At times, being a Bournemouth fan must feel like living in a simulation.

That was certainly the case on Thursday night as the Cherries beat seven-time continental champions AC Milan 3-0 in only their third-ever European fixture.

Justin Kluivert scored the opener at Vitality Stadium, 31 years after his father, Patrick, scored the winning goal for Ajax against Milan in the Champions League final.

Having seen their club narrowly avoid the jaws of liquidation in 2008 , not many Bournemouth fans would have dreamed that famous name would one day appear on their shirts.

"It's mega. In terms of the story of the club it's ridiculous. Someone told me today, 15 years ago today we were 17th in League One, so it's pretty incredible," Bournemouth midfielder Ryan Christie told TNT Sports.

"So many of these fans have been here for this journey so to have nights like this and win as well is special."

To add to the peculiarity of the situation, Milan fielded more English players in their starting XI (three) than the hosts (two).

While the sending off of Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan killed the contest after 27 minutes, Bournemouth were by far the better side up until that point.

In truth, that didn't come as a surprise, even though Bournemouth have won just six points from seven league games this term while Milan are fourth in Serie A.

The three sides they have beaten this season - Real Sociedad, Sturm Graz, and now Milan - have all competed in the Champions League inside the past three years.

For them it's a fairytale, but for the rest of Europe, is it a Premier League-induced nightmare?

Five months after a missed Arsenal penalty denied a Premier League clean sweep in the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League, is this yet another sign of English club dominance?

Bournemouth sweep aside 10-man Milan in Europa League

English clubs played nine games in Europe this week, losing just once.

In fact, Premier League clubs have lost just four of 26 games played across the three continental competitions so far this season. Manchester United are responsible for two of them.

In the five seasons since the Conference League was introduced, no league has yet won all three, but in three different seasons Premier League clubs have won two of them.

Over the past two seasons, Premier League clubs have played 21 knockout ties against European opposition in the Conference League and Europa League - and won all 21.

The only two ties they have lost have been to other English teams.

But, despite such dominance, the Champions League still remains elusive for most, with only Manchester City lifting the trophy over the past five years.

So, why are English clubs so dominant in Europe's secondary competitions - and why hasn't this transferred to consistent Champions League glory?

Fifteen of last season's 20 Premier League teams featured in the top 30 of Deloitte's 2026 Money List.

It is easy to see why then English clubs appear to be head and shoulders above the rest when it comes to the Europa League and the Conference League.

Premier League clubs earn more than £1.37bn per season in television rights, a figure La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1 could only match combined.

Brighton are easily the richest club in the Conference League this season, while Bournemouth and Crystal Palace both appear in last season's top 30.

Last season Aston Villa beat Freiburg comfortably in the Europa League final, with a revenue more than double the Germans'.

Crystal Palace won the Conference League with a revenue of almost four times more than Rayo Vallecano, the side they saw off in the final.

In 2025, Tottenham beat Manchester United in the Europa League final. In the Premier League, they finished 17th and 15th respectively.

In 2022-23, West Ham finished 14th and won the Conference League.

All the evidence points to the Premier League's collective strength. Take away Europe's richest and England dominates.

The summer transfer window was further evidence of Europe's struggles against the Premier League, with the latter again setting a new transfer spend record of £3.49bn to dwarf their rival leagues.

Of the 20 most expensive transfers completed in the summer only six were not to clubs in the English top flight.

You now have Premier League clubs - away from the traditional big six - beating other top European sides to signings.

Premier League wages are generally higher and the league is increasingly seen as the place to be for a lot of European talent.

"With the exception of some of the global brands within football, and I think you'd look at Real Madrid, Barcelona, PSG and Bayern Munich, the Premier League can outspend anyone and everyone," football finance expert Kieran Maguire said in August.

"A significant proportion of overseas players are now choosing to play in England than elsewhere in Europe because of the wages on offer."

Despite the success of Premier League sides in the Europa League and Conference League, the Champions League is a harder nut to crack.

While Barcelona, Real Madrid and Bayern Munich all lost to English teams in last season's elongated Champions League league stage, it has been a very different story when it really mattered.

Over the past two campaigns, eight of nine English teams have been knocked out by one of the Deloitte Money League's big four, according to the last report produced in January 2026.

Chelsea , Manchester City , Newcastle and Liverpool were eliminated by an aggregate score of 25-6 last season.

No English club appeared in the top four of Deloitte's Money List, with Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris St-Germain leading the way. Three of those have won the Champions League five times between them in the last seven years.

English clubs are certainly very much in the mix for the Champions League, with Arsenal losing last season's final on penalties and Manchester City winning in 2023.

But, with just one English club in the past three finals, the Premier League elite are yet to take their European domination to the very top.

Come May, it could well be Bournemouth , Brighton , Crystal Palace or Sunderland leading the English charge in Europe.

articles.title: Celtic 1-2 Celta Vigo: Hoops suffer third Europa League defeat as Spaniards stun with quick double
articles.summary: Match report as Celtic lose to Celta Vigo in the Europa League; Mika Baur opened the scoring for the Hoops; Javi Rodriguez scored a quick double to put the visitors in front; watch Hibs vs Celtic in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday (12pm kick-off), live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
After an emphatic 7-1 win against Hearts, the Hoops once again showed their struggle to take their domestic dominance into European competition. The defeat leaves them as one of four clubs in the 36-team table yet to register any points.

The Celtic fans were screaming for a penalty midway through the first half when Callum Osmond went down from a push from Javi Rueda. It was just outside the box, with the referee deciding not to award a free-kick.

Mika Baur did give them the lead just after the break as he swept home a deflected cross from Haissem Hassan.

After Liam Scales hit the crossbar, Celta hit back with a quick double.

Javi Rodriguez scored twice in three minutes - a header then an unstoppable drive - to stun the home side who could not find a way back as they suffered another damaging Euro night.

Celtic, four points clear of Old Firm rivals Rangers at the top of the Scottish Premiership, face Hibernian at Easter Road on Sunday (kick-off 12pm) - live on Sky Sports.

12: BLOCK! Colby Donovan is well placed to clear Javi Rueda's cross as Celta Vigo look to open the scoring.

15: BLOCK! Mika Baur is in the right place this time to stop Iago Aspas' effort.

23: PENALTY APPEALS! Callum Osmand is pushed as he ran into the box, but the referee is having none of it. Camilo Duran is booked for his protests.

43: CHANCE! The ball falls to Osmand outside the box after Duran failed to get his shot away. He sends it well over the bar.

44: SAVE! Ferran Jutgla is denied by Sam Johnstone with half time approaching.

47: GOAL CELTIC! Haissem Hassan sends in a dangerous cross, it takes a deflection and breaks to Mika Baur to fire in.

52: CHANCE! Aleix Febas meets Sergio Carreira's low cross only to send it past the post.

63: OFF THE BAR! Liam Scales inches from doubling Celtic's lead. The defender gets his head to Hassan's cross, but it hits the woodwork.

68: GOAL CELTA! Javi Rodriguez meets the free-kick and his header can't be saved by Johnstone.

72: GOAL CELTA! A brilliant strike from Rodriguez, a nightmare for Celtic.They fail to clear the danger and he fires in from outside the box.

85: SAVE! Forrest sets up Donovan, but his effort lacks power and it's easily saved.

Sky Sports' Luke Shanley was watching at Celtic Park:

Celta were worth their win. The stats don't lie and they had many more chances than Celtic.

The home side were ahead though and what will annoy them is not being able to see it out. Losing two goals in the space of three minutes was a hammer blow.

Martin O'Neill might not be happy with the award of the free-kick that led to the equaliser, but ultimately they needed to defend it better.

Celtic have now lost four European games in a row. The frustration or the worry is that Celtic are not competing enough at this level and can't bridge the gap after winning 7-1 at the weekend in the Scottish Premiership against Hearts.

Their Europa League campaign is all but over but their misery in Europe might not be.

articles.title: Bournemouth 3-0 AC Milan: Penalties and Amine Adli's free-kick help Cherries to historic Europa League win as Mike Maignan sent off
articles.summary: Match report as Amine Adli caps memorable win for Bournemouth after Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier penalties; Cherries down seven-time champions of Europe; Ruben Amorim's AC Milan reduced to 10 when captain and goalkeeper Mike Maignan shoved Tyler Adams in the face
articles.body:
Ruben Amorim's side are far from the standard of the great Milan teams of the past but this is nonetheless a treasured scalp for Bournemouth who, for the majority of their history, could not have imagined they'd play this fixture. The seven-time European champions, humbled by the Cherries.

It was a wet and wild night on the south coast, with the weather fitting for the chaotic first half, which included Milan captain Mike Maignan being sent off for brutally pushing both hands into Tyler Adams' face at a corner.

That recklessness from the goalkeeper brought Bournemouth their second penalty, which was expertly dispatched by Marcus Tavernier after Justin Kluivert had slotted in the first spot-kick following a Koni De Winter handball.

Another dead-ball moment brought Bournemouth's third. It was a wonderful whip from sub Adli - but Amorim would not have been happy with the Milan wall which broke apart to sum up their sloppiness.

'How did we end up here' was the sign on the Bournemouth banner before kick-off. Their supporters would have been in even further disbelief with their side two-up against 10 men before half-time. By full-time they were gleefully taunting Amorim, who has now failed to beat Bournemouth in five attempts. It was a miserable return to England for the former Manchester United boss.

But it's lift-off at Bournemouth now, after they recorded their first Premier League win of the season over 10-man Sunderland at the weekend and go third in the Europa League table with a perfect record of three from three.

Key moments from the Vitality Stadium...

5: PENALTY! After a VAR check, the officials spot a handball from De Winter, who had his arm up and connected with the ball when Evanilson headed wide.

8: GOAL! Kluivert coolly sends Maignan the wrong way to side-foot into the other corner for a historic early opener for Bournemouth.

28: RED CARD & PENALTY! Maignan is shown a straight red for shoving Adams in the face as Bournemouth send a corner into the Milan box. After a VAR check and plenty of confusion, Bournemouth are awarded another penalty as well!

32: GOAL! Tavernier steps up this time but it's the same result - he sends replacement goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani the wrong way to put Bournemouth into dreamland.

57: CLOSE! Moments after De Winter is forced to clear the ball over his own bar from close range, Kluivert whips the follow-up short corner narrowly wide of the far post.

67: OVER! Sub Rayan rises high but sends his header from Ben Gannon-Doak's cross over the bar.

84: GOAL! Adli whips a free-kick through the Milan wall and into the net to cap a brilliant night for Bournemouth.

87: SAVE! Rayan takes a crossfield pass into the box with his chest - and then is denied a goal by Torriani's fingertips.

articles.title: Besiktas 2-2 Crystal Palace: Jean-Philippe Mateta and Yermey Pino strike but Palace forced to settle for Europa League draw in Istanbul
articles.summary: Match report as Crystal Palace end two-game losing run with a 2-2 Europa League draw away at Besiktas; Wilfred Ndidi put Besiktas ahead before goals from Yeremy Pino and Jean-Philippe Mateta; Junior Olaitan equalised before Umit Akdag was sent off for a bad tackle on Jorgen Strand-Larsen
articles.body:
Mateta thought he had opened the scoring with the first chance of the match when he swept home in the fifth minute, only for VAR to intervene and rule the striker had strayed marginally offside.

Besiktas took the lead against the run of play when Wilfred Ndidi rifled in on the stroke of half-time with Besiktas' first shot on target.

But Palace equalised six minutes after the restart when Pino got on the end of Anan Khalaili's cutback to sweep in. The flag went up for offside, but this time VAR intervened in Palace's favour with the visitors drawing level.

And four minutes later they went ahead after Mateta intercepted a loose back pass before striding into the area and smashing home into the roof of the net.

But Besiktas were back level in the 73rd minute when substitute Junior Olaitan shot low and hard and into the corner.

Umit Akdag was sent off for a two-footed lunge on Jorgen Strand Larsen, before the striker went off injured late on, as Besiktas held on for the draw.

45+1: GOAL! Ndidi smashes home on the stroke of half-time to give Besiktas the lead against the run of play.

51: GOAL! Pino sweeps home but the whistle goes for offside! VAR takes a look and the goal is given!

55: GOAL! Mateta produces an emphatic finish with his first goal since the UEFA Conference League final!

73: GOAL! Substitute Junior Olaitan Besiktas fires in an equaliser to bring Besiktas level!

78: RED CARD! Umit is sent off for Besiktas after a two-footed lunge on Strand Larsen!
